name: The same blood with a clustered loss planted
about: PLANTED: a constructed example, not a person. A clustered loss was planted in a healthy array. Every site of IAM-Atlas v2.1 has one fixed place on this globe, the same as on the atlas's cell pages. Drag to turn it. The healthy reference is healthy blood for this person's own cell mix (IAM-Atlas v2.1, Stage D21 shares), compared at 773,556 sites. The change is fixed by the measurement, never by the reader: each site's difference is measured in that site's healthy width and the sample's own spread, and read in blocks of 10 neighboring sites, as the C-Score reads them; a block has changed beyond the line pure chance crosses less than once in 20 genomes. Ordinary wear is scattered and seldom moves a whole block, so a healthy sample stays nearly dark; a change that runs along the genome lights up in clumps. The slider only quiets the background. A picture: nothing is scored from it; Met-A and the C-Score read against their own commissioned reference, which is also a layer. In a woman one X chromosome is held methylated, so her X can differ from a reference that pools both sexes.

layers.name: the change from the healthy reference
layers.hint: Slide right to quiet the healthy background: its colors drain to gray, then to dark, until only the change is left lit. Slide left to bring the full map back.
layers.fixed: Changed: 45 of 77,355 blocks of 10 neighboring sites, 1 of them on the X and Y chromosomes. This count is fixed; the slider never changes it. Sex not read by Stage 0. The atlas's healthy reference pools women and men. A woman holds one X methylated, so her X can differ from it by nature; the count on the X and Y is shown so a reader can see how much of the change sits there. At Met-A's 6,000 neutrophil sites alone: 44 of 597 blocks changed. A loss of the neutrophils' pattern sits there, too few sites to show on the whole genome: choose the layer "the change at Met-A's 6,000 sites" to see it.
layers.note: Against healthy blood for this person's own cell mix (IAM-Atlas v2.1, Stage D21 shares). Each site's difference is measured in that site's healthy width (how much healthy people vary there, and how sure the atlas is), in this sample's own spread, and read in blocks of 10 neighboring sites, as the C-Score reads them. A block has changed beyond the line pure chance crosses less than once in 20 genomes. Ordinary wear is scattered and seldom moves a whole block, so a healthy sample stays nearly dark; a change that runs along the genome lights up in clumps. Red: more methylation than healthy; blue: less.

layers.key_up: Red: more disorder (entropy) here than Met-A's purified-array reference: the held pattern is being lost, whether the sites started methylated or unmethylated
layers.key_down: Blue: less disorder than the reference: the pattern held more tightly than healthy (rare)
